player.replaces: the joystick read, while the demo flag is set
player.value_shape: one byte shaped like the joystick port: bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire, all active low.  Bits 5-7 are never tested, which is what leaves room for the two-byte opcodes
player.step: one input read by the player state machine, i.e. one pass of the state step, which runs every step_period frames (8 walking, 6 leaping, 15 knocked down)
player.countdown: each read decrements the step counter; while it is non-zero the held value is returned unchanged
player.abort: the real fire button is polled first; pressing it stops the game loop and asks for the main menu.  The keyboard is never polled

opcodes.effect: return this joystick value for exactly one step
return this joystick value for `steps` steps
same as $80-$BF; the opcode band is split by the $C0-$C5 cases
start tune `tune`, then decode the next opcode in the same call
one busy-wait of about two thirds of a second, then one idle step
`units` such busy-waits, then one idle step
end the script: hand `room` to the outer loop, stop the game loop, return one idle step.  The pointer is deliberately left on the operand
ask the outer loop to print intro text page `page`, stop the game loop, return one idle step
force the REST bell delay currently running to finish on its next iteration, then one idle step
clear the demo flag and return "no input"; neither script uses it
